query: Which material can be used for improve the magnetocaloric properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount of interstitial nitrogen into the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high‐entropy alloy will enhance its magnetocaloric properties.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast, equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high‐entropy alloy showing standard magnetic responses.
generation.intervention: Interstitial doping via controlled nitrogen incorporation during alloy processing (e.g., by adding a nitrogen source in the processing atmosphere).
generation.conditions: Measurements performed under controlled thermal cycling and applied magnetic fields at ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Interstitial nitrogen atoms that modify the local lattice environment and induce additional lattice distortion.
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen atoms occupying interstitial sites are expected to alter the local electronic structure and magnetic exchange interactions; this may increase the magnetic entropy change during field-induced phase transitions by tuning the balance between magnetic order and disorder.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increased magnetocaloric effect as indicated by a higher magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) and possibly a shift in the Curie temperature compared to the undoped baseline, with a predicted enhancement on the order of a modest percentage (e.g., a 10–20% improvement) if the interstitial content remains within solubility limits.
generation.baseline: The magnetocaloric properties of the undoped equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA as reported in standard processing conditions.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected only if the level of nitrogen doping does not exceed the solubility limit; excessive nitrogen may lead to the formation of secondary phases or embrittlement, which could negate the improvement.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the magnetocaloric enhancement is uncertain without experimental calibration, and the influence of processing conditions on interstitial distribution must be clarified.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples from the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA: one without interstitial doping and one with controlled nitrogen doping. Subject both sets to identical processing protocols and then measure the magnetocaloric response under the same magnetic field sweeps and thermal cycling conditions.
measurements: Magnetic entropy change (ΔSm) under applied magnetic field cycles
Curie temperature determined from magnetization vs temperature curves
Phase and microstructural characterization by XRD and TEM to confirm interstitial incorporation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrogen-doped samples do not show a statistically significant improvement (e.g., at least a 10% increase in ΔSm or a favorable shift in Curie temperature) relative to the undoped baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
